# Re-dumped after aligning the pitch feature normalization with the OpenSV+
# z-score convention: (value - mean) / standard deviation. The fork's
# multiplication by the deviation left the network input out of range.
# Re-dumped with the Rust NeuralVocoder (a bit-exact port of the C++
# model_vocoder "nhv" path) against the GUMI AI voice. The voice archive itself is proprietary and
# stays behind OPENSVR_TEST_VOICE; only these small text goldens are committed.
# The `in`/`durations`/`pitch` sections below are the acoustic golden
# `acoustic-low.txt` verbatim: the test re-predicts durations (timing), the F0
# curve (pitch) and the acoustic frames with the Rust stages, then renders
# the waveform from the golden acoustic frames so stage
# tolerances cannot stack. The `acoustic` section keeps only the first 20
# frames of the 200-frame dump (waveform goldens grow at hop 240), and
# the `waveform` section (`waveform <frames> <hop> <sample-rate>`, one
# sample per line) is the C++ vocoder output for exactly those frames.
# Acoustic-model golden for opensvr-voice (Phase 5, acoustic stage).
# Re-dumped with the Rust AcousticModel (a bit-exact port of the C++
# model_timbre_pred "dds" path) against the GUMI AI voice. The voice archive itself is proprietary and
# stays behind OPENSVR_TEST_VOICE; only these small text goldens are committed.
# The `in`/`durations`/`pitch` sections below are the pitch golden
# `pitch-low.txt` verbatim: the test re-predicts durations (timing) and the
# F0 curve (pitch) with the Rust stages, quantizes durations onto the 5 ms
# acoustic grid, maps MIDI pitch to log-F0, and compares the `acoustic`
# section (`acoustic <frames> <channels>`, one 72-channel line per frame).
# Pitch-model golden for opensvr-voice (Phase 5, pitch stage).
# Re-dumped with the Rust PitchModel (a bit-exact port of the C++ f0model-dds
# path) against the GUMI AI voice. The voice archive itself is proprietary and stays behind
# OPENSVR_TEST_VOICE; only these small text goldens are committed.
# Input lines start with "in " (<language> <midi> <seconds> <phoneme>...),
# followed by the timing stage's real predicted durations and the expected
# per-frame absolute MIDI pitch (5 ms grid from time zero).
